market_sizing.target_buyer: Founder. Almost universally owner-operated in AU until $1M+ revenue, where a head of production sometimes joins.
market_sizing.business_count_au: Estimated 150-300 commercial fermented-food producers in AU (sauerkraut, kimchi, kefir, yoghurt, miso, water kefir, vinegars). No central census. Visible brands: Kehoe's Kitchen (QLD), Gutsy Ferments (QLD), The Fermentary (VIC), Guty Kefir, Bird Tree Farm (Bottled Culture), Peace Love & Vegetables, Buchi, Eumarrah, Phamish, Gut Feeling Ferments. Long tail of farmer's-market sellers (200-500 add'l) below MRP threshold. [uncertain]
market_sizing.business_count_secondary: US: 800-1500 (Wildbrine, Cleveland Kraut, Farmhouse Culture, Hosoo, Lacto Pickling). UK: 100-200 (Vadasz, The Cultured Collective, Loving Foods, Mother Foods). NZ: 30-60 (Be Nourished, Pickled Pink). CA: 80-150 (Pyramid Ferments, Karthein's). All [uncertain].
market_sizing.typical_size: 1-8 employees, AU$100K-$1.5M annual revenue. Median ~AU$300K. Cottage-industry tail under AU$100K is large but unlikely to buy MRP.
market_sizing.growth_trend: AU fermented food & beverage market 7.10% CAGR 2025-2033 (IMARC). AU prebiotic/probiotic foods 15.80% CAGR 2025-2033 to USD 9.9B (IMARC). 70%+ of probiotics share goes to dairy/fermented foods. Functional gut-health is one of the fastest-growing AU food sub-categories. Independent ferment brands are gaining shelf space at IGA, Harris Farm, Drakes, and woolies independents.

fit_and_timing.addressable_window: Now. Lot tracking ships pre-launch which is the only hard gate. No excise like alcoholic ferments.
fit_and_timing.roadmap_dependency: None hard. Xero integration strongly desired (almost universal in AU food SMB). Wholesale invoicing + price-tier support useful. Cold-chain expiry tracking is helpful — Manuva's lot+expiry already covers this.
fit_and_timing.typical_tier: Starter ($99) for sub-AU$300K producers; Growth ($249) is the natural home; Pro ($499) only for those with national distribution.
fit_and_timing.regulatory_burden: 3 — FSANZ Standard 1.2 labelling, state food-business licence + council registration, batch traceability for recalls, allergen management. Lighter than supplements/TGA, heavier than candles/cosmetics.
fit_and_timing.time_to_value_days: 10-14 days. Workflow is simple — ingredient + jar/lid/label BOM, batch yield, lot tracking through fermentation cycle, wholesale pricing.

economics.incumbent_pricing: Spreadsheets + Xero is the default for 70-85% of the segment. Craftybase $59-199/mo for hobby graduates. Katana $199-359/mo for the larger end. Unleashed NZ$319-399. Cin7 Core $349+. Ekos is too brewery-flavoured for vegetable ferments and rarely seen. Kehoe's-tier producers (top 5%) run MYOB Exo or NetSuite.
economics.willingness_to_pay_aud: AU$99-249/mo realistic. Sub-AU$500K producers anchor heavily on Craftybase pricing. AU$249 Growth tier is justifiable once wholesale + lot tracking + Xero are all needed.
economics.estimated_arpu_aud: AU$170/mo blended (mix of Starter and Growth).
economics.expansion_revenue_potential: 3 — Tier expansion as producers add national-distribution wholesale. Add-on for FSANZ recall-drill reports could be a Pro upgrade. Multi-location expansion (commercial kitchen + co-pack site) drives Pro tier.
economics.churn_risk: 3 — Farmer's-market-stage businesses fold often; once a brand is in 50+ independent grocers, retention is strong (typical food-SMB 3-5% monthly churn). Founder burnout meaningful in cottage segment.
economics.cac_estimate_aud: Cash CAC AU$40-100; founder-time CAC ~3-5 hours per close (light onboarding once template BOMs exist) at $150/hr = $450-750. Blended AU$500-850.
economics.multi_channel_count: 2-3 — farmer's markets + D2C web + wholesale to independent grocers. Some add Faire (now in AU).

Instagram tags #fermentedfoods, #ausferments, #gutsyferments. Reddit r/fermentation (~430K global). LinkedIn AU Food Innovation Centres groups.

outreach_fit.cold_outbound_feasibility: 4 — Brands are tiny, websites list founder + email, Instagram DMs are well-received. AFMA member lists publicly available. LinkedIn coverage is partial but improving.
outreach_fit.inbound_content_fit: 5 — 'How to build FSANZ-ready batch records for a fermented-foods business', 'Sauerkraut BOM template for Australian producers', 'Craftybase vs Manuva for ferments' are all clean SEO targets with low competition.
outreach_fit.founder_market_fit_proxy: 4 — Ferment-segment founders trust outsiders more readily than supplement/cosmetic chemists. Process is craft-based but not credential-gated. Solo founder can land logos with a working BOM template and a Xero integration story.
outreach_fit.case_study_acquisition_cost: Low — first 5 references reachable within 4-6 weeks via direct outreach to known indie brands + AFMA newsletter. Visual case-study material (glass jars, ferment cellars) is plentiful.

foot_in_door_fit.trial_to_paid_benchmark: Estimate 20-30% for CC-required 14-day trial. Free-for-3-months extension to half-price-for-12 likely converts 35-45% if Xero integration is included. [uncertain]
foot_in_door_fit.recommended_foot_in_door_motion: Founder-led outbound + 14-day CC-required trial. 2-3 early design partners (free 3 months in exchange for FSANZ recall-drill feedback + logo). Co-marketing with AFMA newsletter and Sustainable Table. Inbound funnel through 'Craftybase alternative for ferments' + 'FSANZ batch traceability' SEO. Faire/Open Food Network adjacency is a partner-channel angle worth testing.
foot_in_door_fit.rollout_phase: Phase 1 (months 0-3). Fully addressable today; low founder-credibility bar; good case-study material; high overlap with adjacent food segments (packaged foods 11, kombucha 13).

competitive_context.current_dominant_tool: Spreadsheets + Xero (70-85% of segment). Craftybase (5-15% — Indie tier graduates). Katana (3-7% — those who came from a cross-vertical referral). Unleashed (2-5%). Cin7 Core (rare, only at Kehoe's scale). No dominant vertical-specific tool exists for fermented foods. [uncertain] on splits.
competitive_context.switching_pain: 2 — Migrating from spreadsheets to Manuva is straightforward; recipe count is low (typically 5-25 SKUs); main pain is wholesale customer + pricing-tier setup.
competitive_context.competitor_gaps_for_this_segment: Craftybase: low order-line ceiling at $89 Indie tier, weak wholesale invoicing, no lot expiry. Katana: per-seat painful, no native Xero AU, weak on cold-chain expiry. Spreadsheets: no audit trail, no recall-drill reports. Manuva's full lot+expiry+wholesale tier-pricing combination at AU$249 is a clean wedge that nothing else offers at this price point in AU.
competitive_context.user_satisfaction_signals: Reddit r/fermentation and AU artisan-food FB groups carry frequent 'spreadsheet alternative' posts. Craftybase Indie-tier complaints about order-line cliff ($89→$199) appear in user threads. No major Capterra/G2 dataset for fermented-foods specifically — too niche. [uncertain] on direct quotes.
competitive_context.competitor_concentration: Highly fragmented — no tool above 15% share.
competitive_context.integration_dependency_list: Xero (critical), Shopify (D2C), Faire AU, Open Food Network, Australia Post / Sendle (cold-pack shipping), Klaviyo, Square / Tyro (farmer's market POS), Stripe.

partner_channels.industry_association_sponsorship: AFMA newsletter ~AU$200-800/issue; AFMA conference sponsorship AU$1-5K. Slow Food Australia partnerships ~AU$1-3K. Sustainable Table newsletter ~AU$300-1000. Naturally Good Expo small-stand AU$3-7K. AFGC membership ~AU$5K/yr (large for solo founder). [uncertain] on exact 2026 rates.

profitability_math.realistic_12mo_customer_count_solo: 8-15 paying customers in 12 months. Low onboarding friction + addressable today + warm community channels make this one of the better solo-founder bets.
profitability_math.path_to_first_3k_5k_mrr_aud: Pair with indie cosmetics (01) and candle/soap (04) to make the AU$3-5K target. Path: (1) direct outreach to 30 visible brands in months 0-2 → land 3 design partners free for 3 months; (2) ship Xero integration and ferment BOM template; (3) AFMA newsletter feature + Sustainable Table guest article months 3-4 → 4-6 inbound trials; (4) convert 2-3 of design partners + 4-6 inbound to paid Growth tier; (5) by month 12: 10 customers × AU$170 ARPU = AU$1,700 MRR from this segment alone.
profitability_math.customers_needed_for_1m_arr_aud: ~490 customers at AU$170 blended ARPU. Plausible if Manuva becomes the default 'Craftybase replacement for fermented foods' in AU/UK/NZ over 3 years.
profitability_math.solo_founder_bandwidth_fit: 4 — Onboarding is light (template BOMs do most of the work). Support load mostly Xero-mapping questions and wholesale pricing-tier setup. Solo founder can serve 15-25 active customers in this segment without strain.
profitability_math.break_even_contribution_months: 4-6 months (cash CAC only); 7-9 months with loaded founder time.
profitability_math.gross_margin_sensitivity: Low — workflows are simple, support questions are predictable, and founders are accustomed to figuring things out from documentation. Effective GM 78-82%.
profitability_math.priority_ranking: 2 — Strong Phase-1 candidate. Lower ARPU than cosmetics or coffee but higher close-rate and lower bandwidth cost. Earned-community channel (AFMA + Slow Food) is solo-founder friendly.
profitability_math.risks_and_notes: Risks: (1) ARPU ceiling — many brands genuinely belong on Starter $99 long-term, capping segment MRR. (2) Cottage-industry churn — sub-$200K-revenue brands fold or pivot 12-18 months in. (3) Faire AU adoption could deflate need for wholesale-tier features. (4) Craftybase could ship its own AU pricing fix and close the wedge. Verify before going hard: AFMA actual newsletter pricing for 2026; Faire AU connector demand; whether Open Food Network producers (~1500 AU farms+makers) are a partner-channel inroad; specific Craftybase Indie→Business defection volume in AU.
